Your body produces collagen naturally, but production declines as you age. Benefits of collagen 1. Skin health May improve skin hydration, elasticity and reduce the appearance of fine lines. Some studies show modest improvements after 8–12 weeks of use. 2. Joint support May help reduce joint discomfort and stiffness, particularly in people with osteoarthritis or those who exercise regularly. 3. Hair and nails Some people report stronger nails and less nail breakage. Evidence for improving hair growth is currently limited. 4. Muscle recovery and strength May support muscle recovery and muscle mass when combined with resistance training, particularly in older adults. 5. Bone health Some research suggests collagen peptides may help support bone density, particularly when combined with exercise and adequate nutrition.#goviral #skincare #collagen

Up to the age of 25, collagen is well preserved in our body. From the age of 25 to 40, we lose about 15% of our collagen. From the age of 40 to 50, we lose 20% of our collagen, and from the age of 50 onwards, 30%. Collagen is the most important structural component of the skin, since the skin is the largest organ in our body, weighing between 4 and 9 kg. It is also an abundant protein in our body, formed by several amino acids. There are several ways to destimulate collagen, through biostimulants, through massage and collagen powder. It helps to reduce expression lines, strengthens nails, improves hair volume and shine, strengthens cartilage and joints. In other words, several benefits.
